📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Exchanges » Revolut Lists GoMining Token for UK and European Users.

The move brings the niche utility token to more than 15 million fintech app users under the EU’s MiCA regulatory framework.

Retail fintech giant Revolut has added GOMINING, the native utility token of the digital Bitcoin mining platform GoMining, to its in-app cryptocurrency trading service. The listing enables over 15 million Revolut crypto owners across the United Kingdom and the European Economic Area (EEA) to buy, hold, and trade the token alongside everyday banking services.

Prior to this integration, GOMINING was primarily accessible through crypto-native exchanges such as Kraken, KuCoin, and Bitget.

Industry observers note that the listing builds on an existing payment integration established in 2024 that allowed European customers to fund GoMining accounts via Revolut Pay. It also adds GOMINING to Revolut’s cryptocurrency trading service.

Recent findings suggest that revolut reviews digital assets before listing them, assessing their risks, compliance requirements and potential financial crime exposure. It also monitors listed tokens on an ongoing basis as part of its procedures under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

“For years, there has been a clear line between crypto and traditional finance, and most people stayed on one side of it,” stated Mark Zalan, CEO of GoMining, in a statement announcing the listing. “For GoMining, this listing means our token is no longer only for people who already live in the crypto world.”.

GOMINING has several uses within the GoMining platform. Token holders can use it to pay digital miner maintenance fees, with discounts of up to 20%, buy digital miners on the platform’s marketplace and purchase boosts in Miner Wars, GoMining’s mining game.

It has been revealed that the token also has a governance function. Owners can lock their GOMINING tokens to receive veGOMINING, which gives them voting rights on the allocation of ecosystem rewards.

Revolut customers can now buy GOMINING directly through the app. To use the token on GoMining, they must first transfer it to an external GoMining account.

It has been revealed that the Revolut listing gives GOMINING exposure to a wider retail audience through a mainstream financial app. It also provides another way for people to acquire the token without first opening an account on a crypto-native exchange.

It has been revealed that however, buying GOMINING through Revolut does not provide direct access to GoMining’s platform features. Users must transfer their tokens to an external wallet before using them within the GoMining ecosystem.

  • “The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that elon Musk now claims Cybertruck orders “far exceed” Tesla’s production rate, and that the truck isn’t being killed because it’s unprofitable. It’s his second explanation in three days for ending the pickup.

It has been revealed that the problem is that Tesla’s own numbers say the opposite. The Cybertruck line has been running at roughly a quarter of its installed capacity, and Tesla spent all of 2026 discounting, re-trimming, and repricing the truck to find buyers.

Here’s what Musk posted on X overnight:.

“The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate. We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people. This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.”.

The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate. We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people.This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported… https://t.co/rGmNKV3ILs.

He was quote-tweeting a Tesla fan telling people to “get it while you can.” So yes, this is also a sales pitch.

On Friday, Musk unveiled Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027 “to make room for increased Cybercab production.” That was the first story. Now it’s about “complexity” and “opportunity cost.” Let’s go through it.

Sources indicate that tesla controls its production rate. That’s the flaw in this claim.

Tesla built the Cybertruck supply chain for 250,000 units a year, and its latest shareholder letter still lists more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. In Q3 2026, it delivered 8,295 “Other Models.” With Model S and Model X out of production, we estimated 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks. That’s a 30,000-a-year pace, down 48% year-over-year in that category.

According to recent reports, if orders had been outrunning production at any point this year, Tesla had about 95,000 units of idle annual capacity sitting right there. It didn’t use it.

Sources indicate that and companies with a backlog don’t behave like Tesla did. In February, it offered a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 for “only the next 10 days.” It pulled a single-motor RWD version after just 173 sales. It leaned on Musk’s own companies too: SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025, about 19% of US registrations that quarter once you add his other firms.

Cox Automotive estimates US Cybertruck sales fell from 14,416 in Q3 2024 to 3,519 in Q1 2026 and 3,744 in Q2. It’s a demand problem everyone could see.

So if orders spiked this weekend, there’s an obvious reason: Musk told the world on Friday that the truck is going away. A last-call rush on a discontinued vehicle is not proof that it was selling.

Tesla has been sitting on Cybertruck deposits it was never going to fill for years.

According to recent reports, musk touted more than a million reservations, and crowdsourced tallies put the list near 2 million by 2023. Its best US quarter, by Cox Automotive’s estimate, was 14,416 trucks. The reservation book was a vanity number, not an order book.

Sources indicate that two weeks ago, Tesla cancelled the Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand and refunded deposits people had paid in 2019. Returning deposits is something Tesla was already doing because it couldn’t sell the truck in those markets, not because it was swamped.

In a recent development, this one is a straw man. Our reporting, and most of the coverage Friday, was about sales, not margins. The truck sells at about 12% of the volume Tesla planned for.

Tesla doesn’t disclose Cybertruck margins, so Musk can say whatever he wants here and nobody can check it. But he’s the one who said in 2023 that Tesla had “dug our own grave with Cybertruck” because of how hard it was to build profitably.

In a recent development, and look at what Tesla did the same day it unveiled the end of production: it raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the cheapest trim. The cheapest orderable Cybertruck went from $69,990 in early August to $92,490. You do that to squeeze margin out of the last trucks, not because the line was printing money.

Follow Musk’s logic to the end. If the Cybertruck were profitable and orders really outran production, killing it would mean walking away from guaranteed profit for a robotaxi that had 463 units registered in Texas as of late October and no proven business yet.

It has been revealed that the only way that trade makes sense is if the Cybertruck’s profit at 30,000 units a year is small. Which is another way of saying it doesn’t sell enough.

Giga Texas also has more than 10 million square feet of floor space, and the Cybercab runs on its own “unboxed” line. Tesla can’t make use of the Cybertruck line and floor space was never the constraint. To further adapt his logic for shutting down Cybertruck production, Musk shifted his argument from “space” to Cybercab’s line needing some “smart people”, who he implied work on the Cybertruck.

In a recent development, musk wrote on Saturday that “there are a very limited number of smart, dedicated people”, but Michael So, who led Cybercab new product introduction and was Giga Texas employee #1, left in April for nuclear startup Aalo Atomics. Last month, Tesla lost its Cybercab general assembly lead to Rivian’s R2 program just weeks after the launch. If talent is the bottleneck, it’s the Cybercab team that’s bleeding it.

Musk doesn’t want the Cybertruck to go down in history as a flop, and we get it. It’s his truck. He approved the controversial design, hyped it for four years before it shipped, and boasted that 1 million reservations could translate to 500,000 units a year.

In a recent development, but you can’t run a line at a quarter of capacity, run “10 days only” discounts, pull trims after 173 sales, and sell trucks to your own rocket tech giant, then turn around and tell people demand was never the problem. The data is public. Tesla’s own delivery reports are public.

In a recent development, our read on what happened is simple. Demand collapsed in 2025 and never came back. Tesla tried every pricing trick it had. When nothing worked, it found a future-facing reason to end it, and now it’s spinning the inevitable end-of-life rush as proof the truck was a hit all along.

Musk loves a substantial TAM. SpaceX’s IPO filing put its total addressable market at $28.5 trillion, and last month he went further, writing that he sees “a path to SpaceX being worth orders of magnitude more than the current Earth economy.”.

According to recent reports, so apply the same lens to Tesla. Pickups are one of the biggest and most profitable vehicle markets on the planet. Ford sold 801,525 F-Series trucks in the US last year, GM sold 925,656 Silverados and Sierras combined, and Ram moved 374,059. That’s more than 2.1 million trucks from three automakers, easily north of $100 billion a year at today’s transaction prices.

Its funny that such a "free speech absolutist" won't disclose something as simple as auto only OpMargins...proving my point that Tesla post-Musk buyout simply existed to make products that were eligible for EV and green tax credits.

Industry observers note that robotaxis? Waymo, by far the leader, is doing about 500,000 paid rides a week, and analysts estimated its revenue run rate at roughly $355 million earlier this year. Tesla doesn’t even break out robotaxi revenue and we expect it to be a fraction of Waymo’s.

Maybe that flips one day. But that’s the bet here: Tesla is walking away from a giant market it can sell into today for one that only gets substantial if autonomy is solved in the next couple of years. Musk has made that exact bet before. He promised a million robotaxis on the road by 2020 and has remarked unsupervised self-driving was a year away almost every year since 2016. He’s lost every time.

It has been revealed that and that rush is real, for what it’s worth. Some people want the last of a weird, genuinely impressive truck. That doesn’t make it a business.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.

The network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers. Satoshi Nakamoto welcomed users on the forum and invited any questions people had regarding the cryptocurrency.

In 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity. In May, Laszlo Hanyecz probably had the most expensive pizza dinner in history, considering how much BTC rallied after that. By December, Satoshi made their final BitcoinTalk post and revealed their farewell.

It has been revealed that the 2011-2014 period turned out to be the foundation for the network as a whole. Bitcoin became an open-source project maintained by others. The first halving happened in November 2012 and reduced the block issuance from 50 to 25 BTC per block.

The first-ever exchange implosion, Mt.Gox in 2014, raised serious questions about the security and stability of centralized exchanges, an problem we haven't solved 17 years later.

In a recent development, 2017-2021 were the years when the industry truly blossomed. We had our first bull run on Bitcoin, which pushed the price above expected levels, to almost $20,000 in December 2017, along with the first altcoin bull run and the birth of fresh technologies like smart contracts, NFTs and many more. The next cycle took Bitcoin to around $69,000 in November 2021.

However, with the growth of the industry, multiple conflicts arose around safety, integrity and usage. The first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin was El Salvador, which implemented the digital currency as a true means of payment, in addition to accumulating it in its treasury.

2022 was the pivotal year, marked by the FTX and Terra crashes that changed how investors treat markets in general. FTX wasn't just an exchange: it was the backbone of the cryptocurrency market in those years. It aimed to rival Binance and become the bridge between institutional investors and crypto.

However, poor risk management, challenges with fund allocation and many other factors caused an implosion that ended the bull run.

Industry observers note that in 2024, Wall Street arrived in crypto with ETFs, ETPs, perpetual futures and a regulatory framework. The digital assets industry became a part of a larger market. Whether that is good or bad is a question to consider, but one thing is clear: Bitcoin has come a very long way since 2010 and is evolving to this day.

The next step is the arrival of AI and rising cybersecurity risks, which go toe-to-toe with the quantum danger. How the first cryptocurrency handles them is a question that directly affects its future.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, tesla is launching its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its eighth city, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles.
  • Industry observers note that but if Tesla’s recent maps are any guide, a big chunk of that area won’t be bookable.
  • Tesla’s official Robotaxi account made the announcement just after midnight local time: “Robotaxi available in San Antonio starting tomorrow, 5am.” It came with a map of the “launch geofence,” a large polygon that runs from Loop 1604 on the north side down to just south of downtown.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, tesla is launching its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its eighth city, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles. That’s the biggest day-one map Tesla has ever posted, and more than four times the size of Waymo’s San Antonio service area.

Industry observers note that but if Tesla’s recent maps are any guide, a big chunk of that area won’t be bookable. In Austin, an independent check found the Robotaxi app only accepted pickups and drop-offs in about 59% of the zone Tesla advertises.

Tesla’s official Robotaxi account made the announcement just after midnight local time: “Robotaxi available in San Antonio starting tomorrow, 5am.” It came with a map of the “launch geofence,” a large polygon that runs from Loop 1604 on the north side down to just south of downtown.

Robotaxi Tracker, which measures operator maps and logs fleet sightings, puts the zone at 274 square miles. That covers about 1.0 million residents (51% of the metro) and 721,000 jobs. San Antonio International Airport sits inside the polygon, but it isn’t served.

In a recent development, waymo started driverless rides in San Antonio in February with more than 60 square miles and opened to all riders in October, airport trips included. Robotaxi Tracker presently lists Waymo’s San Antonio area at 59 square miles.

What Tesla didn’t say is how many cars will cover its 274 square miles. As of Monday morning, Robotaxi Tracker hadn’t logged a single Tesla Robotaxi in San Antonio.

In a recent development, the launch landed the same day Tesla expanded Austin again. The tracker now measures Tesla’s Austin zone at 443 square miles, up 178 square miles since mid-September.

Industry observers note that we’ve seen this movie. Last month, Tesla expanded its Houston geofence into the shape of a rocket, and within two days the creator of Robotaxi Tracker found the app refusing downtown pickups inside it.

According to recent reports, since then, Koby Pierce, who tracks Tesla’s service on X, has done the tedious work of checking city after city. He searched thousands of real addresses in the Robotaxi app on an emulator and mapped only the ones where Tesla allows a pickup or drop-off, then compared that with the map Tesla advertises. Here’s the share of Tesla’s advertised land area that actually works:.

Austin's dropoff/pickup Geofence is ~41% smaller than advertised.Seems mostly the East side of town is inaccessible. Unsure the cause. Any ideas?Dallas is next and should be done by noon tomrrow. pic.twitter.com/WvU99sJlJh.

It has been revealed that austin is the one that matters. It’s Tesla’s flagship market, with 453 unsupervised vehicles in service according to Robotaxi Tracker. Yet about 41% of the advertised map Pierce tested, mostly on the east side of town, wouldn’t take a ride request. Pierce points to railroad crossings as a major factor in several cities, which lines up with the strange downtown routing we saw in Houston.

Sources indicate that to be fair, Pierce states Waymo is next on his list, and he expects “they’re no better.” Robotaxi Tracker already had to trim Waymo’s Orlando area last month after finding the airport, inside Waymo’s published map, wasn’t selectable. We’ll look at those numbers when they’re out. But it doesn’t change what Tesla is doing with San Antonio today.

Sources indicate that credit where it’s due. A 274-square-mile launch in a fresh city is progress, and Tesla now runs unsupervised rides in eight cities. At the start of this year, it had no unsupervised rides anywhere.

Industry observers note that but we need to stop taking Tesla’s geofence numbers at face value, and that includes us. We used Tesla’s 254-square-mile figure for Houston, and it turned out to be overstated. In all six cities Pierce has checked, the real service area is between 59% and 78% of what Tesla posts. In Austin and Miami, it’s about 60%.

So the honest way to read the San Antonio announcement is “up to 274 square miles.” In practice, expect something closer to 160 to 210 square miles, with an unknown number of cars, and the airport already off the table. That’s still bigger than Waymo’s 59 square miles in the city.

According to recent reports, these maps are mostly fiction. I live inside the Houston map but the app says I am outside. If you drive to where the app allows, no vehicles are ever available. Waymos are a routine site and are available on a short notice. This is smoke and mirrors to shore up the company value ahead of the SpaceX merger.

Sources indicate that the problem is that square miles are the metric Tesla fully controls. Drawing a polygon costs nothing, and the numbers were all over X within hours of the post. Cars per square mile, wait times, and rides completed are much harder to inflate, and nationally Waymo still runs over 4,000 driverless vehicles to Tesla’s 666, per Robotaxi Tracker.

I still consider this a small pilot by any standard, and safety remains the bottleneck. Tesla is still forcing riders through hour-long rides that should take 15 minutes because they have to take routes that avoid areas that Tesla can’t safely navigate without supervision.

Until that’s fixed, robotaxi won’t be able to meaningfully scale beyond these limited demonstrations in geo-fenced areas.

Robotaxi or not, most EV charging still happens at home, and pairing it with rooftop solar can cut your cost per mile to nearly zero. Major crypto exchange Coinbase shared the options-implied seven-day ratios for major cryptocurrencies, highlighting that options traders might be preparing for an unusually large price move for XRP.

In an X post, Coinbase Markets shared the outcome of dividing the options-implied 7-day move by the median 7-day move for XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana.

According to recent reports, options-implied 7d move, divided by each asset's own median 7d move: $XRP 1.94× $BTC 1.69× $ETH 1.56× $SOL 1.46× $XRP is priced furthest above its own history, $SOL the least. Which one is asking for more than its own history delivered? https://t.co/WgWbqjcgwI.

This suggests how much movement options markets are pricing in relative to each asset's own historical behavior. However, it does not compare their expected dollar or percentage moves directly.

Sources indicate that according to the figures shared by Coinbase, XRP's options-implied seven-day move stands at 1.94 times its own historical median seven-day move. Bitcoin follows at 1.69 times, while Ethereum records 1.56 times and Solana comes in at 1.46 times.

XRP, therefore has the highest relative reading among the four assets, suggesting options traders are pricing in a more pronounced move than the token has typically delivered over a comparable period.

At the time of writing, XRP was down 1.93% in the last 24 hours to $0.98 amid the continued profit-taking in the market. XRP briefly reached $1 on November 18, 2026, but fell afterwards as traders took profits. XRP is down 21.57% so far in November, but its history states more than its current price action does.

XRP’s average November gain is skewed upward by massive outlier rallies—specifically +550% in 2013 and +282% in 2024. Its median November return is about -10%, meaning it has closed lower in most cycles in history. XRP dropped roughly 23.42% in November 2019 and lost 12.18% in November 2025 (opening at around $2.51 and closing at around $2.20).

A weak November doesn’t always mean a weak December: for instance, after falling 9.1% in November 2015, XRP jumped 46.8% in December 2015.

According to recent reports, in the near term, XRP’s price recovery will target $1 before moving to the $1.24–$1.26 range. Alternatively, if the price falls further, it is likely to find support at $0.89.

LiveWire just showed off its biggest electric motorcycle lineup yet

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1056 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that liveWire has spent the last few years expanding beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
  • I stopped by the LiveWire booth at EICMA 2026, where the tech giant had everything from its upcoming lightweight S4 Honcho models to the freshly acquired DUST electric dirt bikes – plus STACYC’s electric balance bikes for the youngest riders.
  • It’s quite a spread, and perhaps more importantly, it paints a picture of a firm that increasingly wants to have an electric two-wheeler for just about every stage of a rider’s life.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that liveWire has spent the last few years expanding beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off. But seeing the company’s latest machines all together at EICMA in Milan really drives home just how much broader LiveWire’s ambitions have become.

I stopped by the LiveWire booth at EICMA 2026, where the tech giant had everything from its upcoming lightweight S4 Honcho models to the freshly acquired DUST electric dirt bikes – plus STACYC’s electric balance bikes for the youngest riders.

It’s quite a spread, and perhaps more importantly, it paints a picture of a firm that increasingly wants to have an electric two-wheeler for just about every stage of a rider’s life.

I also had a chance to spend several hours test-riding the S4 Honcho Street in Milan, so be on the lookout for that article and video to experience it with me.

But for now, let’s see what was at the LiveWire booth.

Perhaps the most crucial bikes at the booth were the S4 Honcho models, LiveWire’s fresh lightweight and lower-cost electric motorcycles.

The production S4 Honcho Street made its European debut at EICMA alongside the dirt-oriented S4 Honcho Trail. The Trail version recently began reaching customers in the US, with the Street now en route to dealerships, and European sales are beginning around the EICMA launch.

These bikes represent a significant departure from LiveWire’s earlier strategy. Instead of trying to compete directly with full-size gasoline motorcycles on outright performance, the Honcho platform is aimed at riders looking for something smaller, simpler, and more approachable.

And now the family is getting even bigger.

Also on display was the new S4 Honcho Skate, making its first public appearance.

The Skate is planned for 2027 and further expands the modular Honcho platform with a stripped-down, playful design.

For those who have followed H-D’s electric ambitions for as long as I have, you might even remember the original Harley-Davidson electric moped prototype that seems to have served as inspiration for the Honcho Skate’s design.

In a recent development, seeing the various Honcho versions together also makes LiveWire’s strategy with the platform much clearer. Rather than creating one small electric motorcycle, the company is building an entire family around the concept.

The other major attraction at LiveWire’s booth was the DUST lineup.

Recent findings suggest that liveWire acquired the assets of DUST Moto earlier this year, bringing the lightweight electric dirt bike organization under its umbrella. EICMA marked the first public showing of the production-intent DUST Hightail under LiveWire ownership.

It has been revealed that the Hightail had already generated plenty of interest before the acquisition as a lightweight, high-performance electric dirt bike. Now we’re getting our first look at how that machine fits into LiveWire’s broader plans.

The tech giant is targeting a 2027 introduction for the production Hightail.

LiveWire also showed the new DUST Spur, another model planned for 2027 and intended to expand the newly formed DUST family.

The DUST acquisition is particularly interesting because it gives LiveWire an immediate foothold in the rapidly growing lightweight electric off-road motorcycle space without having to develop an entirely upcoming platform from scratch.

In what could be a hint at faster charging to come, there was an interesting S2 Alpanista Corsa motorcycle that had been outfitted with a NACS plug and DC fast-charging capabilities.

LiveWire claimed a 20-80% charge in under 10 minutes, which would revolutionize the ability to do long-distance motorcycle touring, or just make it more convenient to get a quick charge and head back to your apartment.

There’s on word on whether the concept will make it to production, but the specs are enticing!

The most interesting part of LiveWire’s EICMA display may not have been any individual motorcycle, but rather what happens when you stand back and look at the entire booth.

Sources indicate that on one end you’ve got STACYC electric balance bikes. LiveWire notes the brand has already introduced more than 250,000 riders to two wheels.

Sources indicate that then you’ve got the lightweight S4 Honcho family. Above that sit the DUST machines for more serious off-road riding, while LiveWire’s existing S2 motorcycles continue to cover the higher-performance street end of the spectrum.

That’s becoming something of an electric two-wheeler ladder.

A kid can theoretically start on a STACYC, graduate into increasingly capable electric two-wheelers, and eventually wind up on a proper electric motorcycle – all within the same corporate family.

And that feels particularly relevant at a show like EICMA, where much of the motorcycle industry is still trying to figure out exactly where electric motorcycles fit.

LiveWire seems increasingly convinced that the answer isn’t simply to build electric replacements for existing gasoline motorcycles.

Instead, the company is spreading out into categories where electric drivetrains can create different kinds of motorcycles altogether.

I’ve been following LiveWire’s evolution for years, and the manufacturer standing in front of me at EICMA looks considerably different from the one that started out selling a single expensive flagship electric motorcycle.

The massive, high-performance bikes are still vital, but machines like the S4 Honcho and DUST Hightail are arguably more interesting to me because they can bring entirely different riders into electric motorcycling.

They’re smaller. They’re simpler. And perhaps most importantly, they’re targeting the kind of fun, accessible riding that doesn’t require superbike levels of performance.

There’s still plenty we need to learn about several of these new models, particularly final specifications and pricing for the 2027 machines.

But seeing the Honcho, Honcho Skate, Hightail, Spur, and STACYC machines together at EICMA makes one thing pretty clear: LiveWire isn’t just trying to sell a few electric motorcycles anymore.

It’s trying to build an entire electric two-wheeler ecosystem.

Home » Shiba Inu (SHIB) » SHIB Targets Multiple Billions Via America’s Strike Event.

Despite substantial deleveraging across markets, Shiba Inu earns a comfortable spot at USA’s price-calling giants.

Industry observers note that shiba Inu’s (SHIB) meme currency just got critical acclaim in major United States Perpetuals markets. Nadex, short for North American Derivatives Exchange, filed a motion to the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), pursuing time-capped price events.

Conducting business as Crypto.com Derivatives North America, the exchange self-certified a Shiba Inu Strike Event Contract under Commodity Futures Trading Commission regulations. This now allows traditional Derivatives market players exposure to cash-settled event bids.

These SHIB price-tracking contracts do not use traditional margin leverage. They are fully prepaid or collateralized, so the maximum loss per contract is limited to the price paid to enter (plus fees). There is no margin call or unlimited downside in the style of Perpetual Futures.

By this strategy, Shiba Inu’s been placed within an honorable roster of major-cap altcoins. The exchange also submitted strike event contract notices covering blue-chips like XRP, Solana, Stellar (XLM), Dogecoin (DOGE), Litecoin (LTC), Hedera (HBAR), Ondo & Polkadot (DOT).

The new Shiba Inu (SHIB) price-linked product is a binary-style swap that lets traders take a position on whether SHIB’s benchmark price finishes above a chosen strike at time expiration. Contracts are eligible for listing since November 13, 2026. Will that lift SHIB’s sloppy volumes?

The popular Japanese guard dog-encrusted meme currency saw a tremendous drop in Spot and Futures markets during Q3 of 2026, pushing the meme coin to dwell at upcoming yearly lows. With the Derivatives markets piquing their interest in SHIB, a multi-billion influx could come.

According to recent reports, right now, the trading volumes present a grimy picture of $44.56 million in daily Spot trading volume. This puts Shiba Inu at the sixth position in the meme coin category, ranked by 24-hour trading volume. The canine coin’s down 24% in 30 days, while parent chain ETH slid by 25%.

According to recent reports, further on, the 24-hour turnover rate stood below 2%. On Spot markets, turnover counts SHIB trades already completed, while depth describes orders displayed at the moment of the reading. The same capital can trade repeatedly during a day. Low volumes resemble vague demand.

Recent findings suggest that next up is the major demand retest: if Shiba Inu’s (SHIB) $0.00000353 support bubble holds, the next checkpoint revolves around $0.00000515, with the mid-range extending to $0.000006. Traders need to stay alarmed due to the Parabolic Stop & Reverse (SAR) flashing a ‘sell’ signal on the one-day price charts: bottom may not be in yet.

The $0.00000384 is the level to watch.

Meanwhile, key data on Perpetual markets showcase a gradually rising total Open Interest (OI), as leveraged players increase their positions before a presumed drastic price swing. The soft volume hikes haven’t flipped the switch back to bullish.

Long price plays still account for most of liquidations, soaking up $79.81K out of $87.20K in liquidations on SHIB’s regular smart contract.

Bitcoin miner fees hit a 15-year low – Why profit margins are shrinking

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (496 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as 2026 is nearing its end, Bitcoin [BTC] miners are facing growing financial pressure.
  • According to Glassnode’s recent patch, publicly listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their Bitcoin holdings since January 2026.
  • This means that miners are increasingly treating their Bitcoin reserves as a source of liquidity to fund business operations and maybe for expansion into AI data centers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as 2026 is nearing its end, Bitcoin [BTC] miners are facing growing financial pressure. This, in turn has resulted in miners increasingly selling their Bitcoin reserves instead of holding them for long-term appreciation.

According to Glassnode’s recent patch, publicly listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their Bitcoin holdings since January 2026.

This means that miners are increasingly treating their Bitcoin reserves as a source of liquidity to fund business operations and maybe for expansion into AI data centers.

Sources indicate that at the same time, there is also a decline in transaction fee revenue. With 11 months into 2026, Bitcoin miners earned just 912 BTC in transaction fees, the lowest annual total since at least 2011. This is a huge drop compared to 1,720 BTC in 2025 and 15,178 BTC in 2024.

In other words, transaction fees accounted for only 0.63% of total miner revenue in 2026, down from 1% in 2025 and 6.5% in 2023. This is enough proof that demand for Bitcoin block space has weakened, reducing the contribution of this revenue source.

Remarking on the same, CleanSpark CBO Harry Sudock said,.

Like with any commodity production business, it should get harder and thinner margin over time because the lowest cost operators should be the most successful and durable.

In other words, Sudock believes Bitcoin mining will become increasingly competitive over the next decade, with shrinking profit margins favoring operators with the lowest production and electricity costs.

He expects the global hashrate to continue growing, but at a slower pace than in the previous ten years, as mining hardware becomes more efficient and large publicly listed miners explore AI data centers.

He also argued that Bitcoin mining will not depend solely on large public companies, as smaller businesses and privately held miners can operate profitably.

It has been revealed that at the same time, CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju noted that Bitcoin’s average mining cost reached approximately $62,862 in Q3 2026, based on Marathon Digital’s filings. With BTC trading near this level, miners are facing shrinking profit margins and could face potential losses if prices fall further.

However, the relatively high hashrate suggests miners remain committed to the network despite growing profitability concerns.

This comes as Bitcoin miners are shifting their focus towards AI and high-performance computing (HPC), as investors increasingly value their power infrastructure and data centers.

Companies such as Core Scientific, IREN, and TeraWulf are generating significant revenue from AI infrastructure and HPC services, in some cases surpassing their Bitcoin mining income.

However, the Miner Outflow chart suggests that compared with the rest of the year, November outflows are calm.

At the same time, the Miner Reserve chart was at about 1.1925 million BTC at press time. In fact, through October and into November, it moved in a narrow band, roughly between 1.192 million and 1.1926 million.

All in all, miners are roughly holding steady, with small accumulation or lower net selling.

On Nov. 18, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The listing covers the web interface of the Hyperliquid trading terminal at app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade. The HYPE token dropped to around $65.50 on the evening of Nov. 18, and it recovered to $68.79 by midday Nov. 19, according to TradingView data.

In a recent development, according to the entry, the manufacturer claims to provide digital asset trading services on the website, and it has no address on record. Hyperliquid is not licensed by the SFC, and it is suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or actively promoting its services to the public, the regulator mentioned.

In an accompanying warning, the SFC reminded investors that such platforms often lure consumers with "incredible investment opportunities." The SFC also reminded investors that clients of unlicensed platforms have no legal protection if a platform is hacked or misappropriates their assets.

In a recent development, on the same day, the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority with seven recommendations on the country's new crypto rules. "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity," the group wrote.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 16, two days before the SFC added Hyperliquid to the list, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan spoke at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum. "Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter," Chan said.

According to Chan, the bill will cover crypto dealers, custodians, advisers and asset managers. "Decentralisation does not mean less accountability," he stated.

In April, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial as the first stablecoin issuers in the city, out of 36 applicants in the first round.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Blitz news » Anthropic’s Record $81B IPO Is Here—Will It Test Crypto?

The Claude maker priced shares at $83 for a $1.5 trillion valuation as Bitcoin dips 1.5% ahead of Nasdaq trading.

Anthropic has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share, raising roughly $81.3 billion in the largest public market debut in history—just as digital asset markets pull back and traders weigh whether the historic AI listing will siphon retail and institutional liquidity away from crypto.

According to Anthropic’s official announcement, the Claude AI developer priced its shares roughly 6.4% above its previously marketed range of $70 to $78, assigning the company a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion. Trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT is set to begin Thursday, November 19.

While Wall Street absorbed the massive tech offering, the broader cryptocurrency market traded lower on Thursday morning.

Total crypto market capitalization dropped 1.3% over the past 24 hours to $2.253 trillion, with Bitcoin (BTC) falling 1.5%, the most among the other top 10 biggest cryptos. Bitcoin is currently trading at $63,585.

Anthropic has expanded its IPO to 980 million shares, up from the initially planned 825 million, following exceptionally strong demand from institutional and retail investors.

Priced at $83 per share, the public offering is expected to raise approximately $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion base offering in June and setting a upcoming record.

The company is also raising an additional $26 billion through a private placement of non-voting shares, priced at the same $83 per share. Reported strategic investors include Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC. Combined, the public offering and private placement are expected to generate more than $107 billion.

Retail investors have been allocated up to 20% of the public offering, representing approximately $16.2 billion. Demand has been particularly strong, with total orders reportedly reaching nearly seven times the number of shares available, according to CNBC.

The deal values Anthropic at approximately $1.5 trillion, marking a dramatic increase from its $965 billion private valuation when it confidentially filed for an IPO in June.

Anthropic’s IPO could have implications for crypto markets beyond the AI sector. The $155 billion in combined IPO capital raised by SpaceX and Anthropic within five months highlights growing competition for institutional liquidity, potentially diverting funds from risk assets such as Bitcoin and altcoins.

The listing also gives retail investors a direct way to bet on AI, potentially reducing demand for crypto-native AI tokens that have attracted investors seeking similar exposure.

Recent findings suggest that ANT’s market debut will also be closely watched as a gauge of risk appetite. A strong opening could lift sentiment across speculative assets, while a weak performance could reinforce risk-off sentiment in both equities and crypto.

#52865. I Analyzed 30 AI ‘Doctors’ on Social Media and Couldn’t Believe What I Found

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (889 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Menshealth ↗ Open Full Page

I Analyzed 30 AI ‘Doctors’ on Social Media and Couldn’t Believe What I Found

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At least, that’s what a doctor on social media told me.
  • It has been revealed that there’s just one problem: The doctor doesn’t exist.
  • It has been revealed that you’re probably thinking that you’d never fall for such an obvious scam, but AI-generated content is growing increasingly sophisticated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I HAVE YEARS’ worth of poop in my intestines.

At least, that’s what a doctor on social media told me. He was wearing a white coat. His diplomas hung on the wall behind him. Ominous music played in the background while he performed a graphic demonstration about how one product can clean my gut of all that fecal matter, leaving me feeling healthier, happier, and less “toxic.”.

It has been revealed that there’s just one problem: The doctor doesn’t exist. He was created by generative artificial intelligence to sell a product.

It has been revealed that you’re probably thinking that you’d never fall for such an obvious scam, but AI-generated content is growing increasingly sophisticated. And unless a social post comes labelled as “A.I. content,” you might never know these virtual characters dispensing health advice aren’t human.

Recent findings suggest that to get a sense of how widespread this issue is, I searched TikTok and Instagram for AI-generated health content featuring fake doctors and other medical professionals. I wanted to see what sorts of information they were giving, if they were selling products, and if there was a transparent disclosure of the use of AI to create that content.

Recent findings suggest that I quickly identified 30 accounts that featured AI-generated doctors and health influencers. Some of these accounts were not marked as AI content. Others had the blue Meta verification check that’s supposed to mark an account as authentic and credible. But how can someone be authentic and credible if they don’t exist?

What I found was shocking—but there are still a few critical tells you can use to sniff out a scam.

TAKE, FOR EXAMPLE, the curious case of James Anderson.

In a recent development, in September 2026, an Australian fact-checking organization discovered hundreds of Instagram ads featuring an AI-generated surgeon by that name. Anderson was supposedly from Newly introduced Zealand, Australia, and even Toronto, depending on the ad. In Canada, the content identified him as Dr. James Anderson, MD, FRCSC (Orth). FRCSC is Fellow of the Royal College of Surgeons (Canada), a regulated credential that was clearly being hijacked.

His pitch was simple and hopeful: Instead of surgery for your sore shoulder, you should consider a device called Mendable Shoulder. The device, allegedly developed by Anderson and a “team of biomedical engineers,” could heal your pain in just 12 minutes a day, according to the pitch. It cost $119, but was cheaper if you bought three. Some of these ads claim that Anderson works at North Toronto Shoulder Clinic, which, as someone who actually lives in North Toronto, I’ve never heard of—because it doesn’t exist.

Whoever created Anderson dreamed up an entire persona for him, complete with a convincing appearance, fabricated credentials, made-up experience, and fake testimonials.

It has been revealed that even real doctors aren’t safe from having their names and likeness scraped by these companies to sell products. A recent investigation by CBC News found hundreds of online videos using deepfakes of real medical professionals whose faces and voices had been stolen and manipulated to make them appear to endorse products and services that they’d never recommended.

NOT ALL THE accounts I studied relied on fake credentials or white coats and fabricated diplomas. Some featured elderly, AI-generated characters who were allegedly sharing “ancient remedies” and old “secrets” from other cultures.

A large proportion of these supposed “remedies” were absurd or even sexist, calling breasts “hooters” or showing a model of a vagina with “worms” coming out of it. All of them told viewers that modern medicine had forgotten about—or hadn’t yet discovered—this special cure. One simple remedy can solve all of your health problems, was a common refrain. Some of these accounts linked to Amazon pages selling supplements or books. Others were clearly going for clicks and views. Which brings up the next red flag...

According to recent reports, THE MOST SURPRISING detail I noticed was how popular these accounts appeared to be. Several had follower counts in the millions, which only serves to increase their perceived value and credibility.

Recent findings suggest that although some of the engagement on the posts probably came from bots (or at least, I want to believe that they are), there had to be some real people in there, too. And real people are certainly encountering this content, and potentially using it to help make decisions about their health. But don’t mistake popularity for authority.

MY INFORMAL SEARCH wasn’t a scientific study. But larger investigations suggest that AI-generated experts are an increasingly sophisticated vector for health misinformation.

In 2026, Spanish fact-checking organization Maldita found 250 AI-generated health accounts reached more than 53 million followers across seven languages.

They also identified 25 Instagram accounts impersonating medical professionals. Collectively, these accounts had more than 3.6 million followers and had accumulated more than 397 million video views.

So remain skeptical, especially when a so-called “expert” or “professional” talks about “ancient remedies,” supplements, or treatments that involve basic foods that are found in your kitchen.

And if they offer a link to buy supplements from their Amazon store, back away. If it sounds too good to be true, or even just seems “off,” ask your doctor or another IRL health professional.

Abby Langer, RD is the owner of Abby Langer Nutrition, a Toronto-based nutrition consulting and communications firm.

According to recent reports, according to SoSoValue data, U.S. Ethereum spot ETF flows totaled -$77.23 million as of the 16th of November. This week’s ETF outflows reflected bearish sentiment in the market.

The 7-day average Binance USDT reserve was $29.71 billion, which was once again in the 1st percentile of the past year, with a Z-score of an even more astonishing -3.37.

It has been revealed that the values meant that, compared to the past year, the ETH, and USDT reserves were at an annual floor. The Z-score drew further attention to the anomaly; readings beyond ±2.0 are major statistical outliers.

The analyst also noted that the outflows were concentrated on Binance, as all-exchange flows of ETH were only down 2.1% in a month, compared to Binance’s 11.3% drop.

It is possible that the Binance ETH outflows were going toward self-custody or staking. The record staking numbers reflected long-term investor belief despite recent price losses.

Lowered stablecoin reserves also indicated reduced buying power on Binance. Overall, the falling stablecoin and ETH reserve were a cautious combination, but the next price move’s direction is not yet confirmed.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin’s push to position ETH as a store of value was another hopeful sign for long-term investors.

BYD unveiled the Yangwang Altior, its upcoming ultra-luxury EV with coach doors, over 1,000 km of CTLC range, a 1,000V fast-charging platform, and plenty of premium extras.

The “super-luxury executive flagship sedan,” as BYD calls it, made its official debut in Abu Dhabi, UAE, over the weekend.

For those who don’t know, Yangwang is BYD’s ultra-luxury sub-brand, sitting at the very top of its brand hierarchy.

The Atrio is Yangwang’s largest and most luxurious sedan, set to compete with high-end brands like Rolls-Royce, Bentley, and Mercedes-Benz Maybach.

Measuring 5,600 mm long, 2,030 mm wide, and 1,590 mm tall, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase, BYD’s flagship sedan sits squarely between the Rolls-Royce Ghost and Phantom (standard wheelbase) in length.

BYD mentioned the “Golden Body Proportions” are designed to maximize interior space for both front and rear passengers.

Its meticulous front-end design is inspired by “Ding,” a traditional ancient Chinese cauldron, featuring “diamond-cut” headlights, a 137-gemstone dot-matrix grille, and, to top it off, a 24K pure gold car emblem sits up front and center.

The coach doors create a grand entrance, with the front doors opening at an 80-degree angle and the rear doors opening to a 90-degree angle.

Inside, the flagship sedan takes luxury up a notch with a massive, full-length panoramic center infotainment screen that extends from the driver to the passenger side.

The “Wrap-around cockpit” is designed to create an immersive, premium experience, with four executive seats and a central island for rear passengers that includes vehicle controls, storage, and even a champagne glass holder.

BYD said it offers the most second-row space in its class, but didn’t reveal specifics. The zero-gravity “cloud-like” rear seats feature a four-ball mechanical massage head, you know, for those longer trips.

Meanwhile, the front passenger seat can fold at the push of a button to open up more space for rear passengers.

The interior features premium materials, including full-grain genuine leather seats, diamond-cut detailing, real wood trim, and natural lambswool foot pads.

Sources indicate that and that’s not all. It also has a 39-speaker Dynaudio Platinum Evidence high-end sound system that creates an immersive 360-degree “hall-level” sound experience.

The Yangwang Altio is packed with BYD’s latest breakthrough tech, including a high-speed tire-blowout stability system, emergency float mode, and in-place U-turn or tank-turn control using its quad-motor e4 platform.

It's main rival is the Maextro S800, which wasn't in the list.

It also uses BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Fast Charging Technology, which provides a CLTC driving range of over 1,000 km (621 miles).

The flagship sedan features “extremely fast flash charging,” BYD said, thanks to its 1000V ultra flash charging tech. It takes just five minutes to charge the vehicle’s battery from 10% to 70%. To go from 10% to 97% it takes just nine minutes.

BYD opened orders for the limited-edition “Mountain and River Rhyme” Yangwang Altrio model, which will be extremely exclusive with just 399 units.

Buyers can place a reservation with a 300,000 yuan ($45,000) deposit. BYD didn’t reveal final prices, but the global version is expected to start at around 2 million yuan ($300,000).

Binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review.

To protect its users and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts regular reviews of all listed spot trading pairs; it may delist certain spot trading pairs for various reasons, including low liquidity and trading volume.

Binance will delist GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY and ZAMA/TRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18.

Four of the five affected pairs are related to the Turkish lira (TRY), while the last one is HBAR/BNB. The decision affects trading between these specific assets and does not mean the cryptocurrencies themselves are being completely delisted from Binance.

The exchange clarified that consumers will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform.

Binance will terminate Spot Trading Bots services for the spot trading pairs simultaneously where applicable. Customers are strongly advised to update and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots prior to the cessation of services for Spot Trading Bots to avoid any potential losses.

In a recent development, in related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process.

Industry observers note that affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in consumers’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default.
  • AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, new research reveals.
  • A fresh report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical people into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default.

AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, new research reveals.

A fresh report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical people into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.

The research paper combines public GitHub data on open-source projects, a survey of Bitrue users, and profiles of eight active bots to show where automation is heading.

Public GitHub activity reveals a clear change in focus. New repositories describing themselves as “trading agents” jumped from 110 in 2024 to 1,133 in 2025 and reached 6,121 through November 15, 2026, more than five times the prior year’s total.

Classic crypto trading bot projects also grew sharply, rising from 551 in 2024 to 2,399 in 2025 (a 4.4× increase) with another 2,948 created so far in 2026.

The longest-running open-source tools still dominate stars: Freqtrade (56,933), Hummingbot (21,231), Jesse (8,807), and OctoBot (6,951).

An industry survey of 3,708 crypto traders published by MEXC in October 2026 found that 84.8% had used AI for research or trading in the previous six months, with 53.1% doing so at least weekly.

Among AI users, 34.6% had used an exchange’s own strategies or bots and 17.1% had connected an external agent.

On one major multi-exchange platform, average daily bot launches rose 29% from July to September 2026, reaching 862 per day, with real-fund launches up 36% and DCA bots up 80%.

The report identifies five structural changes:.

Recent findings suggest that in Bitrue’s survey of owners who had not yet tried an AI trading bot, concern about losses and risk control was the top reason for hesitation (45.5%). Other common reasons included not trading futures yet (27.3%) and simply not knowing the feature existed (22.7%).

Industry observers note that willingness to let AI trade rose from 55% when only notifications were offered to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage, and losses were in place. Only 6.5% of respondents said they would allow AI to control more than half their account.

In a recent development, among non-consumers, the most requested first steps were a clearer explanation of what the bot does (27.3%) and a trial reward for the first trade (22.7%). Half of those who had not tried an AI bot noted they were ready to do so; another 36.4% wanted to learn more first.

According to recent reports, users who had already tried Bitrue AI most often cited time saved from watching charts, automatic execution, and market analysis as the main benefits. Requests for improvement centered on more trading pairs, flexible parameters & alerts tied to indicators such as RSI.

The report profiles eight systems that illustrate different approaches:.

According to recent reports, AI automation continues to expand, but adoption still hinges on control. Crypto traders want to see why a strategy was chosen, know the maximum loss, test it first, and understand connection security and costs.

Tools that explain their reasoning, enforce user-set boundaries, and allow small or reversible starts are the ones positioned to convert interest into regular use. The report does not forecast specific outcomes beyond these observed trends.

According to recent reports, the numbers show both rapid builder activity and cautious but growing trader demand. The gap between the two is being closed by guardrails, explanations, and simpler interfaces rather than by handing full control to AI.

#52855. Latest Update: Musk admits Tesla doesn’t have enough talent to build more than one car at a time after exodus

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1737 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Musk admits Tesla doesn’t have enough talent to build more than one car at a time after exodus

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, elon Musk now says Tesla can’t build the Cybertruck and the Cybercab at the same time because there are only so many “smart, dedicated people” to go around.
  • It’s the most honest explanation yet for how Tesla went from five consumer vehicle programs at the start of 2026 to a single platform, Model 3 and Model Y, by the middle of 2027.
  • On Friday, Musk noted Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around the middle of next year “to make room for increased Cybercab production.” As we pointed out at the time, Giga Texas isn’t short on space.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, elon Musk now says Tesla can’t build the Cybertruck and the Cybercab at the same time because there are only so many “smart, dedicated people” to go around. Half the executives he demonstrated off in 2023 as proof of Tesla’s “bench strength” have since left the manufacturer.

It’s the most honest explanation yet for how Tesla went from five consumer vehicle programs at the start of 2026 to a single platform, Model 3 and Model Y, by the middle of 2027.

On Friday, Musk noted Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around the middle of next year “to make room for increased Cybercab production.” As we pointed out at the time, Giga Texas isn’t short on space. The Cybertruck line runs at a fraction of its installed capacity because the truck sells a fraction of what Tesla planned.

A day later, replying to a user on X, Musk gave a different reason:.

“The biggest thing most people fail to understand is that there are a very limited number of smart, dedicated people! They can only do so many things.”.

He added that if Tesla has to “maintain a complex production line, supply chain and allocate engineering for Cybertruck, we can’t use those people” for scaling Cybercab.

Recent findings suggest that by this morning, the explanation had shifted again, to the “opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck.” But the Saturday version is the one that matters. Musk is telling us the bottleneck at Tesla isn’t factory space or money. It’s people.

The Cybertruck is the second casualty this year. In January, Musk announced the end of the Model S and Model X on Tesla’s Q4 earnings call and summed up the reason in one word: “Autonomy.” The Fremont line is being converted to build Optimus robots, and by April, only inventory was left.

Recent findings suggest that the flagships had been on life support for years. Their last real patch was the 2021 interior refresh. The June 2025 “refresh” brought a upcoming paint color, a front bumper camera, a bit more range, and a $5,000 price increase. That’s not how you treat a vehicle program you care about.

Sources indicate that tesla painted a very different picture just two years ago. At its 2024 shareholder meeting, it showed this slide of its lineup: the Model 3, Model Y, Model S, Model X, Cybertruck, and Semi, plus three vehicles under covers that Musk mentioned were “going to be pretty special.”.

Of the five consumer vehicles on that slide, three are now dead or on their way out.

In a recent development, so here’s what will be left in the second half of 2027: Model 3 and Model Y, two vehicles built on the same platform, plus the Model Y L and cheaper “Standard” variants of both. The Semi is a commercial truck. The Roadster’s production is still a giant question mark. And the Cybercab is a robotaxi with no steering wheel, not a car you can buy – even though Tesla is going to let fleet buyers get them to add on its own Robotaxi network. We previously explained how this is a terrible idea.

In a recent development, for comparison, Hyundai Motor Group sells more than half a dozen EV models in the US across its Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis brands, on top of its gas and hybrid lineup. GM and Toyota run dozens of nameplates at once. Tesla can’t keep more than two programs alive at the same time.

At Tesla’s Investor Day at Giga Texas on March 1, 2023, Musk mostly stayed out of the spotlight. Instead, Tesla paraded more than a dozen executives on stage to present its plans, a rare move for a firm long criticized for being a one-man show.

“We’ve obviously got significant bench strength here,” Musk remarked at the time.

Of the 14 executives named as presenters that day, seven are gone:.

Martin Viecha, who ran investor relations through that event, left in April 2024 as well.

Seven are still at Tesla, according to their LinkedIn profiles: Tom Zhu, Lars Moravy, Franz von Holzhausen, Ashok Elluswamy, Karn Budhiraj, Laurie Shelby, and Brandon Ehrhart. And the ones who left weren’t peripheral. They ran batteries, powertrain, software, chips, energy, charging, and the money.

The bigger problem for Tesla’s ability to run vehicle programs is the program-level talent, the people who take a car from prototype to volume production.

Recent findings suggest that in November 2025, Tesla lost the head of its Cybertruck program, Siddhant Awasthi, and the Model Y program manager, Emmanuel Lamacchia, within a day of each other. Lamacchia had led Tesla’s best-selling vehicle for four years.

Then the Cybercab, the program Musk is now pulling people toward, started losing its own leaders:.

Add 17-year finance VP Sendil Palani and Thomas Dmytryk, the director who built Tesla’s over-the-air enhancement system and Robotaxi infrastructure, both in March, and you get the picture.

So when Musk says he needs Cybertruck’s people for Cybercab, part of the reason is that Cybercab keeps losing its own.

Recent findings suggest that musk will frame all of this as focus. Autonomy is going to be so significant, the argument goes, that Tesla has to go all in.

But we’ve heard that before. Tesla made the yoke steering wheel standard on the Model S and Model X in 2021 because the cars would soon drive themselves, then brought back a round wheel as an option. It removed the turn signal stalk from the Model 3 in 2023, then brought the stalk back in 2025 and started selling a $350 retrofit to owners. Each time, the autonomy that justified the change wasn’t there yet.

And Tesla isn’t the leader in unsupervised driving. It has the best driver-assist system on the market, but Waymo still logs roughly seven times more driverless miles per week, and NHTSA estimates Tesla’s entire Robotaxi fleet at about 1,000 vehicles. Zoox is scaling too, and Baidu’s Apollo Go runs a far bigger driverless fleet in China.

This is something that I’ve been highlighting for a decade. Even after it became a major company with a large headcount, Tesla has never been good at running several vehicle programs in a healthy way. The Model S and Model X were starved for updates long before the talent exodus started. Tesla has always thrown everything at its newest program and let the older ones coast.

What changed is that the slack is gone. In 2023, Tesla could still neglect the flagships and keep them on the market, because it had deep benches in engineering, manufacturing, and software to absorb mistakes. Today, half the executives Musk called his bench are gone, and the people running the Cybercab ramp keep walking out. Musk is now openly telling us there aren’t enough people left to build a pickup truck and a robotaxi at the same time.

Sources indicate that musk calls it focus. It looks a lot more like a constraint Tesla can’t hire its way out of.

Industry observers note that tesla never had the capacity to hire, organize, manage and retain the amount of human talent required to develop multiple car model lines in concert. Tesla barely paid its staff enough for one model line development.

It has been revealed that you only need to look at other companies with decades of experience in developing many, separate (but technically strongly overlapping) model lines to see how much does that require in terms of human resources and in terms of R&D cost. Like BMW has always been investing ~5 billion EUR every year in R&D. That is how you have ~14 core models with at least another dozen specialist models and more regional models plus Mini and RR on top. At times up to 60 different significant variants with different drivetrains also impacting design, logistics and production. All being always in development for the next generation and also for a mid-life refresh or two. Across the whole group, including maintenance work, there can easily be triple-digit number of vehicle model projects going at the same time.

And Tesla can not even manage a handful.

It has been revealed that will the Cybercab be revolutionary and make it all worth it? We have our doubts. Tesla leads in driver assistance with FSD, but it has failed to evolve the product into unsupervised self-driving at scale, which it promised to buyers for a decade. It’s clearly not the leader in unsupervised self-driving, and the competition is crowded. Tesla’s lasting impact on the robotaxi market is genuinely hard to predict.

It has been revealed that what’s not hard to see is the trend. Tesla has shown a complete inability to sustain multiple vehicle programs at once, and it’s getting harder for the automaker, not easier. If Tesla can’t hold on to the people who build its cars, how long before the Model 3 and Model Y get the same treatment as the Model S?

Both vehicle programs will undoubtedly go down in history as some of the most critical EVs of all time, but that doesn’t guarantee lasting success in a rapidly changing auto landscape.

If you’re driving an EV, the people building it matter, but so does where your electricity comes from. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • S&P Global Ratings assigned a score of 5 to Tether’s USDT, the weakest in its five-point stablecoin stability scale.
  • This was mainly because there was a growing proportion of higher-risk assets in Tether’s reserves.
  • Notably, the agency also warned that a significant decline in their market value could erode Tether’s reserve surplus and potentially leave it undercollateralized.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

S&P Global Ratings assigned a score of 5 to Tether’s USDT, the weakest in its five-point stablecoin stability scale. What’s more surprising here is the fact that the assessment, which was published on the 18th of November, 2026, has remained unchanged since November 2025.

This was mainly because there was a growing proportion of higher-risk assets in Tether’s reserves. According to S&P Global, these assets accounted for 28% of circulating USDT as of the 30th of September 2026, compared with 24% in 2025.

Notably, the agency also warned that a significant decline in their market value could erode Tether’s reserve surplus and potentially leave it undercollateralized.

According to recent reports, that remarked, Tether’s reserve composition has also shifted over the past year, with gold holdings rising from $12.9 billion in September 2025 to $19 billion in September 2026. Meanwhile, the organization also added $4.2 billion in publicly traded equities, while its Bitcoin holdings declined from $9.9 billion to $8.4 billion.

It has been revealed that yet, despite the growing exposure to riskier assets, Tether reported $191.45 billion in reserves against $183.50 billion in liabilities as of the 30th of September. This in turn left a reserve buffer of approximately $7.95 billion and a collateralization ratio of 104.3%, up from 103.9% in 2025.

Still, above all of this, USDT traded close to its $1 peg over the past year, while its market capitalization grew from $158 billion to approximately $184 billion between September 2025 and September 2026.

However, according to a recent AMBCrypto report, Tether’s market capitalization dropped by $6.6 billion over the course of sixty days, ending on the 7th of November.

Ford’s EV batteries retain more than 90% health after 100,000 miles

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, your electric vehicle battery may last longer than you think.
  • The Mustang Mach-E went on sale in late 2020 as Ford’s first fully electric crossover SUV designed from the ground up.
  • Since launching the 2021 Mustang Mach-E, Ford has been collecting data from over 36,000 vehicles that have traveled two billion miles across the US and Canada.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, your electric vehicle battery may last longer than you think. Ford says its EV batteries retain greater than 90% health on average after 100,000 miles. Here are a few tips to keep yours healthy.

The Mustang Mach-E went on sale in late 2020 as Ford’s first fully electric crossover SUV designed from the ground up.

Since launching the 2021 Mustang Mach-E, Ford has been collecting data from over 36,000 vehicles that have traveled two billion miles across the US and Canada.

According to Ford, the Mach-E’s battery has retained 92% of its health on average over the past five years.

Sources indicate that across its full EV lineup, including the F-150 Lightning and E-Transit, Ford said its battery packs maintain more than 90% health on average after 100,000 miles. The key number to look at is the spread, with 95% of vehicles falling between 87% and 97% health.

Of 2021 model-year EV owners, Ford remarked, more than 2,000 have crossed 100,000 miles with their original battery averaging better than 91% health, while over 30 have crossed the 200,000-mile mark and average 88% health.

Ford is using real-world data to help owners take good care of their electric vehicles, no matter how much they know about batteries and other EV tech.

It’s also applying lessons from developing the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, which will underpin its next-generation EVs, starting with the Fantom pickup next year.

In a recent development, ford offered a few simple, everyday tips to help owners support long-term battery health. For one, if possible, charge at home on Level 2 for daily commuting or driving and save DC fast charging for longer trips.

Recent findings suggest that it also helps to avoid charging in extreme temperatures if you can. Preconditioning the battery can help bring it into the optimal temperature range, while parking in the shade on hot summer days can also help avoid long-term battery degradation.

Last, but not least, you can use the Ford App to find charge-level recommendations designed specifically for your vehicle and battery system.

The 2021 Mustang Mach-E uses an NCM battery, but some newer Ford batteries use a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery chemistry, which is recommended to charge to 100% from time to time.

Ford has introduced upcoming features in the Ford App to help owners maintain battery health specific to their vehicle and will continue to use the data to improve the experience as it introduces its next-gen EVs.

This is an article about Ford EV's, so my comment is kind of relevant.

Recently I picked up a 2017 Ford Focus Electric for my daughter to use when she gets her permit soon. It had 91,000 miles when I got it and now has 92,400 miles. I like driving it enough that I've been driving it and letting my Equinox stay home.

  • Grayscale’s latest report highlights a hidden risk that still catches market-timing investors off guard.
  • Upcoming research from Grayscale demonstrates Bitcoin’s (BTC) volatility has fallen to roughly 43%—lower than nearly one in five S&P 500 stocks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Is Calmer Than 19% of S&P 500 Stocks, But Here’s a Catch.

Grayscale’s latest report highlights a hidden risk that still catches market-timing investors off guard.

Upcoming research from Grayscale demonstrates Bitcoin’s (BTC) volatility has fallen to roughly 43%—lower than nearly one in five S&P 500 stocks.

The catch? Bitcoin’s calmer day-to-day trading hides a massive trap for anyone trying to time dips: almost all of its multi-year gains still come from just a handful of explosive trading days.

In its report, “Beyond Volatility: Rethinking Cryptocurrency Risks,” US digital asset manager Grayscale notes Bitcoin’s long-term performance is heavily influenced by a handful of trading days. Its returns have “fat tails,” meaning sharp gains and losses occur more frequently than in traditional stocks.

Over the past three years, Bitcoin delivered an annualized return of roughly 60%. Excluding its 10 best days would have cut that figure to 7%, while excluding its 10 worst days would have raised it to 197%.

Industry observers note that the report also notes that Bitcoin has historically rebounded sharply after major declines. Since 2011, it has experienced seven drawdowns exceeding 50%, although Grayscale notes these declines are not unusually severe compared with stocks and bonds when adjusted for volatility.

Grayscale also sees Bitcoin as a potential portfolio diversifier because it is less exposed to traditional market factors.

The tech giant points out that Bitcoin has historically recovered sharply after significant declines. Since 2011, Bitcoin has experienced seven drawdowns of more than 50% from previous highs.

The report cites Bitcoin’s inclusion in J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions as a milestone.

Grayscale describes JPMorgan as a $5 trillion investment manager that now examines Bitcoin alongside established asset classes.

The banks’ 10-year base case for Bitcoin projects a 10% compound annualized return for Bitcoin over the next decade, the highest among the asset classes covered. The forecast also assumes 55% annualized volatility and a 33% correlation with US large-cap stocks, the number below international equities, corporate bonds and hedge funds.

In Bitcoin’s early years, volatility routinely exceeded 100% and at times approached 200%, with a market cap in the single-digit billions.

Grayscale ties the decline to roughly 43% to larger market value and liquidity, greater institutional participation, Bitcoin exchange-traded products and regulatory clarity.

In historical tests, modest Bitcoin allocations raised annualized return and Sharpe ratio in a representative institutional portfolio.

In a recent development, over three years, Bitcoin explained about half of return variation across FTSE Grayscale Crypto Sectors. Among the 10 largest non-stablecoin assets, six led quarterly performance over the past two years, while Bitcoin led none.

Sources indicate that JPMorgan’s decision to include Bitcoin in its long-term forecasts, along with declining volatility, could shape how institutions approach crypto investments. At the same time, Grayscale’s data reveals how much Bitcoin’s long-term performance depends on a small number of trading days, highlighting the risks of trying to time the market.
